sentences.text: Enaliornis belongs to the parent group Hesperornithiformes. Because it lacked specific traits found in other hesperornithines, scientists initially classified it as a loon or diver (Gaviiformes).
The largest species, Enaliornis barretti, was about the size of a large pigeon. Enaliornis is believed to have had poorly developed wings.
It remains undetermined whether Enaliornis had teeth, unlike other members of its order, Hesperornithiformes.
Enaliornis likely possessed lobed feet adapted for swimming instead of webbed feet.
The genus Enaliornis was first described by Harry Seeley in 1876. Seeley originally named the genus Pelagornis in 1866, but the name had to be changed because it was already used for a Miocene bird.
Three species of Enaliornis have been described: the small E. sedgwicki, the medium-sized E. seeleyi, and the large E. barretti.
Enaliornis lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage. Fossils of Enaliornis have been discovered near Cambridge, England.
